blocks.text: An interim briefing for the leadership team. The engagement opened on {{fact:f:E-2011-002.start}} and is in its early weeks. This is a read of where the work stands and what we are examining, not a set of conclusions; those come later, and only once the evidence behind them is settled with your people.

items: The current-state read is under way: how the organization is directed today across its main functions.
Nothing here is a recommendation. The design work follows once the present picture is settled.
Deborah Gordon has the map drafted for the two largest functions and is closing the remainder.
Today is about sharing what we are examining and agreeing the questions worth pursuing.
We start by listening, then set down the few judgments the design turns on.
Every recommendation traces back to the evidence beneath it, figure by figure.
Where the evidence supports only a range, we say so rather than round it off to look finished.
Julie Parks, Senior Engagement Manager, runs the engagement and is your point of contact.
Deborah Gordon, Associate, carries the analysis and builds the exhibits behind it.
Sponsored on your side by Julie Gonzalez, Director of Operations, who owns the data requests.
The reporting lines, the spans of control, and the layers between the top of the house and the front line.
What each manager is accountable for, and where two managers believe they own the same thing.
How a handful of everyday decisions actually travel, and where authority sits away from the work.
Where the structure is heavy and where it is thin, against a sensible benchmark.
Close the current-state read across the remaining functions.
Confirm the roles that appear under two managers at once.
Keep data requests flowing through Julie Gonzalez as a single consolidated list.
Agree the two or three questions the design should turn on.
